NutriFresh Foods - Q3 2023 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NutriFresh Foods Q3 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Today's conference is being recorded. At the request of the company, this call is also being webcast live on the internet.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NutriFresh Foods' Q3 2023 results. Joining me on the call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Growth Officer; and David Ruiz, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the safe harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Please refer to our SEC filings, including our most recent Form 10-K and 10-Q, for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Sarah.

Sarah Thompson (CEO):
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3 2023. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on seven key areas: key achievements and challenges in the quarter; organic revenue growth overall and by region; market share trends for major brands; organic sales growth guidance for the next quarter and year; impact of new product innovations and launches; discussion of pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies; and revised or reaffirmed full-year guidance.

Let me start with the key achievements and challenges that shaped our performance this quarter. Our team delivered a resilient quarter amid a dynamic macro environment, with net sales reaching $1.28 billion, up 7.2% year-over-year and 5.1% on an organic basis—our strongest organic growth in three quarters. Adjusted EBITDA came in at $215 million, a 12% increase year-over-year, with margins expanding 110 basis points to 16.8%, driven by disciplined pricing and productivity gains.

On the achievements side, volume growth and market share gains stood out. Total company volumes grew 3.8% year-over-year, outpacing the industry average of 1.2% as reported by NielsenIQ. In our Snacks segment—our flagship NutriCrunch protein bars and veggie chips—we saw a 6.5% volume uplift, fueled by distribution wins at major retailers like Walmart and Kroger, where we gained 1.2 points of ACV share. This mirrors trends at peers like PepsiCo's Frito-Lay, but our advantage came from velocity improvements—up 4% in core markets—thanks to targeted in-store merchandising and shopper marketing.

In Beverages, our reformulated ZeroSugar line, including the new electrolyte-infused SparkVibe sparkling water, drove 9% volume growth. This product has resonated with Gen Z consumers shifting toward functional, low-cal options; IRI data shows it capturing 15% market share in the RTD hydration category within six months of launch, similar to Prime Hydration's debut but leveraging our established route-to-market strengths.

Supply chain and productivity initiatives proved transformative. We realized $28 million in gross savings through our Supply Chain 2.0 program, including automation at our Ohio facility—where ABB robotic palletizers reduced labor costs by 18%—and AI-driven demand forecasting via SAP IBP integration, which cut inventory levels by 12% while boosting on-shelf availability to 97.5%. This offset commodity inflation and positions us ahead of rivals like Mondelez facing similar pressures.

Regionally, North America was our powerhouse, contributing 68% of sales with 9.4% organic growth, bolstered by e-commerce penetration reaching 14% of segment revenue—up from 10% last year—through partnerships with Amazon Fresh and Instacart. In APAC, we grew 12% organically, led by Indonesia and India launches of localized pouch-packaged snacks, capitalizing on the $15 billion shift from street food to packaged goods. Sustainability efforts here included cocoa sourcing from Rainforest Alliance-certified farms in Indonesia, reducing Scope 3 emissions by 22% and earning us a spot on the Dow Jones Sustainability Index for F&B.

Strategically, we're accelerating our health-and-wellness pivot. Plant-based SKUs now make up 28% of our innovation pipeline, with R&D investments yielding 15% sales mix from better-for-you products. This aligns with consumer trends—62% of shoppers prioritize nutrition labels per Mintel—and drove gross margin expansion to 38.2%, up 90 basis points year-over-year.

That said, we faced headwinds. Input cost inflation persisted, with wheat up 14%, sugar 11%, and edible oils 9% year-over-year per S&P Global indices—echoing pressures at Hershey and General Mills. This shaved 150 basis points off gross margins before mitigations, leading to three pricing actions averaging 5-7% across the portfolio, which passed through 85% to consumers without significant volume elasticity.

Consumer softness in premium segments affected EMEA, where sales grew just 2.1% organically against our 6% expectation. Economic pressures in the UK and Germany—amid 8%+ food-at-home inflation per Kantar—dampened premium snack demand, resulting in a 4% volume decline in our Artisanal Bites line. Competitive intensity from private labels, now 28% of category sales, pressured pricing power.

Supply disruptions arose from droughts in Brazil delaying orange juice concentrate, costing our Juice division $12 million in contribution—similar to Coca-Cola's issues. We mitigated with futures hedging, securing 70% of FY24 needs at favorable rates, though it highlights vulnerabilities in tropical commodities.

Labor and FX challenges included wage inflation pushing SG&A up 10% in constant currency, offset by zero-based budgeting. Adverse FX—particularly the weakening euro and peso—shaved 2% off reported growth.

These results affirm our Resilient Growth framework: portfolio optimization by rationalizing 15% of low-velocity SKUs, tech-enabled efficiency, and innovation velocity with 12 new items launched at a 70% success rate. Challenges reinforce agility—we're nearshoring suppliers to North America and piloting precision agriculture with John Deere for wheat yields.

Turning to organic revenue growth overall and by region, we achieved 6.1% year-over-year on a constant currency basis, excluding acquisitions, divestitures, and FX impacts. This marks our ninth consecutive quarter of positive organic growth, outperforming the global F&B industry average of 3.5% per NielsenIQ scans. The momentum came from balanced contributions: pricing at +3.2%, volume gains of +1.8%, and favorable product mix shift of +1.1%, driven by premiumization in health and wellness categories.

North America, 52% of total revenue, delivered 7.2% organic growth. This was powered by strong velocity in our core beverage portfolio—our Zero Sugar Lemonade line saw +12% household penetration per IRI—and accelerated snack sales amid at-home snacking. Premium dairy alternatives like plant-based Fresca Oat Milk grew 18% year-over-year, capturing share from Chobani and Silk as consumers seek clean-label, high-protein options. Pricing held at +4.1% despite PepsiCo's promotional intensity in carbonated soft drinks, with volumes up +2.5% from trade spend optimization and club channel expansion at Costco and Sam's Club.

EMEA, 28% of revenue, posted 4.5% organic growth amid softer sentiment and inflation. Volumes rose modestly +0.9%, but pricing added +3.4%, passing through costs in dairy and snacks without share loss—our Eurozone snack share steady at 11.2% per Kantar. Wins included functional beverage launches like Collagen-Infused Sparkling Waters, gaining +15% distribution in the UK and Germany, tapping post-Ramadan wellness in MENA. Our Farm-to-Shelf sustainability program, with 25% recycled packaging, drove a 3-point mix uplift amid EU regulations.

APAC, 14% of revenue and our high-growth engine, accelerated to 8.9%, the strongest in two years. Urbanization and e-commerce in China and India propelled out-of-home rebound +22% in QSRs. RTD tea portfolio surged +14% on volume, while low-sugar energy drinks gained 2 share points vs. Red Bull. Pricing at +2.8% was moderated by competition, but localized SKUs like mango-flavored kombuchas boosted mix +3.1%. Digital efforts, including Alibaba partnerships and our app for nutrition tracking, drove +30% e-com growth.

Latin America and other emerging markets, 6% of revenue, achieved 5.3% organic growth. Brazil and Mexico led beverages +7%, aided by soccer tailwinds and hydration packs for heatwaves. Volumes +3.2% despite FX, via 40% reduced import reliance from Andean fruit hubs; pricing +1.7%, mix up on premium protein bars.

These results highlight our Flavor Forward strategy: innovation in functional low/no-sugar products (now 35% of portfolio, up from 22% in 2022), AI supply chain agility cutting stockouts 25%, and data-driven pricing like Unilever's. We're gaining 50 basis points global share YTD per Euromonitor. For Q4, we guide 5.5-7.0% organic growth, led by North America and APAC assuming stable costs.

Next, market share trends for our major brands. Drawing from latest NielsenIQ, IRI, internal ACV, and Circana data through Q3 end, our aggregate share in beverages, snacks, and BFY foods hit 14.2% in U.S. measured channels, up 110 basis points year-over-year—strongest gain since post-pandemic. This outpaces legacy CPG contraction of 80 bps average per Kantar, as private labels take 22.5%.

In beverages, PureSpring sparkling waters expanded to 28.4% in flavored sparkling, +240 bps, outpacing LaCroix (down to 32.1%). Velocity at 12.2 turns/week in IRI, up 18%, from Zero Sugar, Zero Compromise with electrolyte variants and 50mg green tea caffeine.

VitalQuench energy drinks grew to 11.7%, +90 bps, taking 1.2 points from Celsius (now 22%). $150M regenerative guarana sourcing enabled Clean Energy claims, lifting household penetration +4.2 points to 28%; North America drove 65%, Midwest ACV to 92% via Kroger/Walmart.

In EMEA, VitalQuench hit 8.9% in Western Europe, +150 bps, with 250ml on-the-go cans for c-stores amid 7% channel shift.

For snacks, NutriCrunch and FreshaFruit hold 16.8% in BFY bars, +130 bps vs. Kind (19.2%) and RxBar (12.4%). NutriCrunch's 20g plant-based bars grew 15% dollar share, repeat rates 62% per Circana via AI flavors like Smoky BBQ Chickpea; HPP extended shelf life 40%.

In APAC, FreshaFruit reached 7.2% in dried fruits urban IRI, +200 bps, via Tmall/Flipkart +28% GMV; dynamic pricing held ASP +1.8% vs. category 4.2%, EBITDA 32%.

Latin America showed resilience; AquaBoost hydration to 13.5% in Brazil RTD, +80 bps vs. Del Valle, via local guava PureSpring family packs +5 points penetration.

Peers struggled: Coke CSDs -1.1 to 42.3%, Pepsi snacks -70 bps to private labels 24%, Nestlé +20 bps amid cocoa +45%. Disruptors like Olipop to 4.2%.

Our pillars: innovation velocity (12 Q3 SKUs, 75% $10M+ run-rate vs. industry 55%, R&D +18% to $220M on precision fermentation); distribution (ACV 89%, 2200 new SKUs in club/e-comm, IBM blockchain cutting recalls 30%); consumer pricing (3-5% hikes, 2.1x pass-through, volume +1.4%). Q4 implies 80-100 bps gain.

Shifting to organic sales growth guidance for next quarter and year. Q3 saw 5.2% organic, from 2.8% pricing in CSDs/RTD coffee, 1.7% volume in plant-protein shakes/zero-sugar sports drinks, +0.7% mix from VitalQuench velocity +12% IRI. Share +110 bps NA non-alc per Nielsen/Circana vs. Pepsi Gatorade/Monster.

For Q4 2024, guide 4-6%, moderating from Q3 lapping pricing comps. Pricing 2-3% for EMEA/LatAm cocoa/aluminum +25% Bloomberg; volumes 1.5-2.5% from 15 PureEssence organic juice SKUs ($12B market +8% SPINS), +20% repeats Costco/Sam's; mix neutral-+0.5%, offsetting legacy CSD cull (8% portfolio).

NA ~60% growth at 5-7%, e-comm 18%; EMEA 2-4% vs. HFSS regs like Unilever; APAC/LatAm 6-8%, China RTD tea vs. Coke Honest.

Full-year 2025: 5-7% organic, high-end of F&B 3-5% McKinsey. Drivers: $250M R&D, 25% sales <3yr launches (adaptogen waters $4.5B nootropics); AgriLink WC to 45 days, vs. Red Sea peers; ACV 95%, CRM +15% basket.

Risks: downtrading/unemployment, coffee +30%; hedge 70% 2025, agile pricing. Confident mid-single EPS CAGR 8-10%.

On the impact of new product innovations and launches, new products drove 28% of top-line growth, $187M incremental revenue vs. 22% Q2, offsetting -1.2% legacy decline, expanding adj gross margins +140 bps to 42.3% via premium pricing.

Beverages: VitaBoost functional hydration (electrolyte zero-sugar sparkling with ashwagandha/lion's mane vs. Prime/Liquid Death) launched Feb, 14K US stores Walmart/Kroger in 90 days, velocity 4.2/wk +35% benchmarks, $92M Q3 (15% bev rev), grew seg 8.7%; Reno aseptic/rPET -18% packaging, 51% margins EU compliant.

Snacks: PureCrunch plant pea/cricket 18g protein bars ($12B market 7.5% CAGR Euromonitor), NA/APAC June launch, 12% high-protein share IRI +3pts Clif/RXBAR clean-label; $64M Q3, 62% repeats Amazon top-5, <4% cannibalization.

$145M R&D +12%, AI flavor/precision ferm Ginkgo natural stevia -22% vs aspartame; 85% bio-films Scope3 -15%, DJSI rank.

NA 42% new sales $112M, func bev 18% cat Beverage Digest, TikTok GenZ +7 pen; EMEA $45M +32% PureCrunch UK/DE Novel Foods cricket Tesco/Carrefour, 44% margins <5g sugar; APAC $22M +55% VitaBoost matcha JP/KO 8K Lotte/Aeon 9% func drink, shio koji 28% convert, India Reliance; LATAM $8M Brazil SaborVivo mango fiber +40% Nielsen Pao de Acucar eco-pouches.

Innovate-to-Dominate: 60/30/10 alloc, 18 annual launches, TreeHouse co-mfg 5x scale, $250M IndieFero kombucha 10% pipeline. Q4 +15% velocity $220M; risks cocoa +45%, Pepsi Poppi; 65% tested, AI 12% cat outperf, +50bps share 2024.

Regarding pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies, these were central to our 5.2% organic net revenue growth in Q3, fifth straight positive quarter for NutriFresh. RGM balances price, volume, mix vs. inflation/consumer shifts.

Waterfall: pricing/mix +7.8% offset -2.6% volume. Pricing + ahead Coke/Pepsi mid-singles, 4-6% list on 85% portfolio since 2023—dairy Premium Milk/plant alts, NutriCrunch—steady promo SKUs.

Elasticity -1.8 NA vs. IRI -2.2 cat avg; premium shift 12% vol value-to-premium zero-sugar func +15 units, RTD coffee +22%, health snacks wellness; mix +1.2pts.

NA 52% rev +9.1% pricing 70% dairy/sugar +18% CME, vol -3.2% private labels Kantar 3.5% grocery, smart dynamic Kroger/Walmart +2-3% yogurt.

EMEA 25% +6.4% HFSS UK/EU, reform 40% snacks sodium +4% no vol loss, mix ambient biscuits +8%.

APAC/LatAm 23% +8.5%, Brazil/India cocoa +45% ICCO guardian 92% pass, vol +2.1% urban e-com Shopee +25% D2C.

RGM CoE AWS SageMaker SKU-store elasticity, trade -15% $120M ZBB, promo AI 12% ROI vs 28% Unilever-like; prune 18% low-vel free slot RTD shakes $250M FY25.

Commodity hedge 70% 2025 wheat +12% oils +22% S&P; 50k panel 62% value, Rewards app +14% repeat. Q4 pricing/mix +7-8%, vol stabilize USDA 2.5%; outperf cat 3-4% Euromonitor.

Finally, on revised or reaffirmed full-year guidance, Q3 built on Q2 $1.35B net rev +8% org (5% vol 3% pricing), adj EBITDA 22.5% +120bps, EPS $0.78 beat $0.05—third accel top/margin amid cocoa +25% Hershey/Mondelez, Oceania dairy.

Raising FY: organic net rev 7-9% prior 6-8%, consol sales $5.45-5.60B -1% FX strong USD; adj EPS $2.95-3.15 +10c mid prior $2.85-3.05, tax 23.5% 185M shares, $500M repurchase 60% YTD.

Drivers: vol ZestEnergy +1.2pts NA Nielsen vs Gatorade TikTok GenZ, NutriBar +12% protein 15% CAGR Euromonitor; pricing 4% YTD value packs pen, input 5-6% prior 7-8% sugar hedge Brazil cane.

Margins 23.0-23.5% +100bps mid, Supply Chain 2.0 $75M ann Wisconsin ferm whey -18%, AI freight -12% NA; 40% rPET EU subs ESG millennials.

NA 65% 9-11% at-home e-comm 18% Amazon/Instacart; EMEA 20% 5-7% HFSS low-sugar Zest -1% Q2 vol; APAC/LatAm 15% double-digit India +15% sachets Brazil +8% soccer.

Imperatives: premiumize 25% BFY +200bps gross Kellogg/GM; digital DTC app 20% repeat omni +25%; M&A $1.2B dry powder adaptogen tea 10%+ CAGR 2027.

Risks: palm oil/port strikes 50-75bps, downtrading <2% ZestBasics. Confident profitable growth F&B leader.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael to provide more detail on our financial results.

Michael Chen (CFO):
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q3 2023. Net sales were $1.28 billion, representing a 7.2% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 38.2%, impacted by input cost inflation but offset by pricing actions and productivity gains. Operating income was $180 million, and earnings per share were $0.92. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $850 million in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

For the full year, we are raising our guidance for organic net revenue growth to 7% to 9% and adjusted EPS to $2.95 to $3.15.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will open the call for questions. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please proceed.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your business?

Sarah Thompson (CEO):
Good morning, John. Inflation remained stubborn, particularly with wheat up 14%, sugar 11%, and edible oils 9% year-over-year per S&P Global—similar to Hershey and General Mills. It shaved about 150 basis points off gross margins initially, but our three pricing actions averaging 5-7% across the portfolio achieved 85% pass-through without meaningful volume elasticity. Combined with $28 million in supply chain savings, we expanded margins overall. We're hedged 70% for FY24 and focused on productivity to navigate this.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

Emily Chen (JPMorgan):
What are your plans for new products and what is the expected impact?

Lisa Patel (Chief Growth Officer):
Thanks, Emily. New innovations like VitaBoost functional sparkling waters and PureCrunch protein bars drove 28% of Q3 growth, $187 million incremental, expanding margins to 42.3%. VitaBoost hit 4.2 units/store/week velocity, $92 million sales; PureCrunch 12% subcategory share. With 18 annual launches from our 60/30/10 pipeline, R&D $145 million, and Q4 targeting $220 million, we expect 50 basis points share gain in 2024, fueling mid-single-digit topline.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Lopez with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

Mike Lopez (Morgan Stanley):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

David Ruiz (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
Good question, Mike. Our Supply Chain 2.0 delivered $28 million savings via Ohio robotics -18% labor, SAP AI forecasting -12% inventory to 97.5% availability. Brazil droughts cost $12 million in juice, but hedging covered 70% FY24. We're nearshoring to NA, precision ag with John Deere, and AgriLink cut WC to 45 days vs. Red Sea issues at peers. This positions us resiliently.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Sarah Kim with Barclays. Please proceed.

Sarah Kim (Barclays):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Michael Chen (CFO):
Thanks, Sarah. Q4 organic sales 4-6%, FY25 5-7% at industry high-end. NA 5-7%, APAC/LatAm 6-8%, pricing 2-3%, volumes 1.5-2.5% from innovations like PureEssence juices. Margins 23-23.5% via efficiencies, EPS $2.95-3.15. Assuming CPI 2.5%, stable freight; hedged inputs mitigate risks. Strong momentum in health, digital.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Sarah Thompson for closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in NutriFresh Foods. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
